questions.question_text:
A line from the top corner of a triangle divides its base into $17\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$. Both smaller triangles have perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$.
Find the difference between their areas in $\text{cm}^{2}$.

options.why: Subtracted $17\times12$ and $9\times12$ without halving either product.
Found the whole triangle's area, $(17+9)\times12\div2$, instead of the difference.
Subtracted the base parts and halved the difference, using $(17-9)\div2$, without multiplying by the height.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{First area}=17\times12\div2$
$=102\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Second area}=9\times12\div2$
$=54\text{ cm}^{2}$
$102-54=48$
The difference is $48\text{ cm}^{2}$.
